newsitem.title: USA: Spectranetics gets FDA okay to test laser.
newsitem.headline: Spectranetics gets FDA okay to test laser.

text.p: Spectranetics Corp said Monday it received conditional regulatory approval to start testing its laser technology to treat blockages in leg arteries.

The company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved testing its peripheral excimer laser angioplasty technology designed to treat total occlusions, or blockages, in leg arteries, at 10 medical institutions.
The company added the FDA conditional approval for testing under an investigational device exemption follows a similar approval in Europe, where it is testing the technology at four sites.
It added the trials are aimed at patients with blockages longer than 10 centimeters for whom medical therapy is inadequate and bypass surgery inappropriate.
More than three million people in the U.S. suffer from peripheral arterial disease, or leg artery blockages, Spectranetics said.
